full_caption: Stonebrook Realty Trust, Appellant, v. Marbury Hollow Holdings, LLC, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Stonebrook Realty Trust appeals the denial by the Rooksbury County Board of Adjustment of a use variance permitting operation of a veterinary clinic at 4368 Bellweather Street, Rooksbury, NR, a parcel zoned R-2 single-family residential.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: A nonconforming use lawfully existing at the effective date of the ordinance may continue but may not be enlarged, and is lost by abandonment or by discontinuance for the period specified in the ordinance.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The parcel is 1,060 square feet, irregular in shape, and burdened by a drainage easement across 10 percent of its buildable area. Those are conditions of the land and not of the owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Discontinuance for 18 months is presumed abandonment under Section 17.9 of the ordinance. The presumption is rebutted by proof of an intent to resume coupled with overt acts consistent with that intent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The board's findings must be sufficient to permit meaningful review. Conclusory recitals tracking the language of the ordinance, without reference to record evidence, require remand.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Exhaustion of administrative remedies is a prerequisite to judicial review. A facial constitutional challenge to the ordinance is excepted from that requirement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: An area variance is governed by a balancing test weighing the benefit to the applicant against the detriment to the health, safety and welfare of the neighborhood, and does not require the showing of hardship applicable to use variances.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Vested rights against a subsequent ordinance arise where the developer, in good-faith reliance on a validly issued permit, has made substantial expenditures. Stonebrook Realty Trust expended $590,000 on site work before the moratorium was adopted.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: A use variance requires proof of unnecessary hardship: that the property cannot yield a reasonable return in any permitted use, that the hardship is unique to the parcel, and that the variance will not alter the essential character of the locality.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Spot zoning is the singling out of a small parcel for treatment differing from that of surrounding property, for the benefit of the owner and to the detriment of the comprehensive plan. The rezoning here served a plan objective and is not spot zoning.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: The denial is vacated and the matter remanded to the Board for findings addressing the drainage easement and the shape of the parcel.

sections.heading: RIDER C — NONCONFORMING USE AND ABANDONMENT
sections.text: A use lawfully existing on the effective date of this ordinance may continue in its then-existing scope but shall not be enlarged, extended to additional land, or changed to another nonconforming use. Discontinuance of the use for 18 consecutive months creates a rebuttable presumption of abandonment, which may be overcome by evidence of an intent to resume together with overt acts consistent with that intent.

sections.heading: RIDER E — APPEAL AND EXHAUSTION
sections.text: Any person aggrieved may appeal to the Board within 60 days of the decision, and thereafter to the Northridge courts within thirty days of the Board's written decision. Administrative remedies must be exhausted before judicial review is sought, except that a facial challenge to the constitutionality of the ordinance may be brought directly.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Governing Law
sections.text: This instrument shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Northridge, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Any action arising out of or relating to this instrument shall be brought exclusively in the courts sitting in Rooksbury County, Northridge, and each party consents to the personal jurisdiction of those courts.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Insurance
sections.text: The party in possession shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence, naming the other party as an additional insured, and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request and on each renewal. Each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds actually received.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Indemnity
sections.text: Each party shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other from all claims, damages and expenses, including reasonable attorney's fees, arising out of that party's use of the subject premises or breach of this instrument, except to the extent caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of the party seeking indemnity. This clause survives termination.
